title: How Heat Becomes a Number Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Diya's digital thermometer beeps and shows 37 degrees. But a thermometer cannot feel anything, so how does it turn heat into a number? The answer is a transducer: a device that changes energy from one form into another, usually a physical quantity like heat, light, sound or pressure into an electrical signal, or back again.

On a live breadboard a thermistor sits in a voltage divider with a fixed 10 kilo ohm resistor across 5 V. As it warms from 25 to 37 degrees, its resistance falls, more current flows and the output voltage on the oscilloscope rises. We see why a negative temperature coefficient thermistor behaves this way, derive Vout = Vs R/(R + RT) step by step and work out the output at body temperature. Then active transducers (thermocouple, solar cell, piezoelectric crystal) vs passive ones (thermistor, light dependent resistor, strain gauge), everyday and hospital applications, the exam trap, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a card to screenshot.

This is Episode 31 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 4: Passive Electronic Components (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
